title: Fix vertical misalignment of group header count badge (lane-tab-count)
description:
In the sidebar group header row (chevron, colored dot, group name, tab-count badge — e.g. "EMBERSTONE  10"), the count number is visibly misaligned vs. the group title's baseline. See attached screenshot.

Root cause: components/WorkspaceLane.js renders the header as a `.lane-header` flex row (meridian.css line ~460) using `align-items: center`, which centers children by box height, not text baseline. `.lane-title` (13px, `padding: 2px 4px`) and `.lane-tab-count` (11px, no padding) end up with different box heights, so their glyphs land at different optical heights. There's already a hardcoded `transform: translateY(1px)` on `.lane-tab-count` (meridian.css ~line 702) — and a similar translateY hack on `.lane-collapse-btn` (~line 554) — attempting to compensate, but it's an imprecise nudge rather than a real fix, hence the visible offset.

Fix: replace the box-centering + magic-number-nudge approach with real baseline alignment — either:
- switch `.lane-header` to `align-items: baseline` and remove the translateY hacks on `.lane-collapse-btn` and `.lane-tab-count`, or
- give `.lane-tab-count` matching vertical padding to `.lane-title` so box heights match before centering, then drop/adjust the translateY nudges.

Verify visually that chevron, dot, title, and count badge all sit on a consistent visual baseline after the fix. Apply to meridian.css (and mirror to meridian-extension/ if that CSS is duplicated there like the other recent background-panel changes).
label: Bug

activity.content:
Fixed the group-header count alignment in both shipped CSS copies.

- Changed `.lane-header` from box centering to baseline alignment.
- Removed the compensating `translateY(1px)` rules from `.lane-collapse-btn` and `.lane-tab-count`.
- Mirrored the change in `meridian-extension/meridian.css`.

Verification: rendered the real CSS in headless Chrome and visually confirmed the chevron, group dot, title, and count share the intended header alignment; `git diff --check` passes; both CSS copies remain byte-identical.
